text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 6 in history:
1189 - King Henry II of England, the first of the Plantagenets, died and was succeeded by Richard I.
1535 - Sir Thomas More was executed for treason after refusing to recognise Henry VIII as the head of the Church of England.
1553 - King Edward VI of England died and was succeeded by Queen Mary I.
1685 - At the Battle of Sedgemoor, in Somerset, England, the troops of King James II defeated the mainly peasent supporters of the Duke of Monmouth. It was the last battle fought on English soil.
1747 - John Paul Jones, naval hero of the U.S. War of Independence, born.
1796 - Nicholas I, Tsar of Russia, born; his reign ended with Russia's defeat in the Crimean War.
1832 - Maximillian, archduke of Austria and emperor of Mexico, born. He was imposed on Mexico by Napoleon III and executed by the Mexicans in 1867.
1885 - French chemist Louis Pasteur successfully treated a patient with his anti-rabies vaccine.
1909 - Andrei Gromyko, longstanding Soviet foreign minister during the Cold War era, born.
1919 - The first airship to cross the Atlantic, the British R-34, arrived in New York.
1923 - Nancy Reagan, wife of former U.S. president Ronald Reagan, born Nancy Davis.
1925 - Bill Haley, rock'n'roll musician and band leader, born. His "Rock Around the Clock" sold an estimated 25 million copies worldwide.
1928 - The first all-talking feature film, "The Lights of New York", was premiered in New York.
1935 - The Dalai Lama, Tibet's spiritual and temporal "God-King", born; he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 for his non-violent campaign to free his homeland from China.
1937 - Vladimir Ashkenazy, Russian concert pianist and conductor and winner of the Tchaikovsky Piano Competition, born.
1942 - Diarist Anne Frank and her family took refuge from the Nazis in Amsterdam.
1944 - A fire sparked by inept fire-eaters in the main tent of the Ringling Brothers and Barnum & Bailey Circus in Hartford, Conn., killed 167 people.
1946 - U.S. film actor Sylvester Stallone, best known for his "Rocky" series of films, born.
1962 - William Faulkner, U.S. novelist and Nobel Prize winner, died.
1964 - The Nyasaland Protectorate became the independent state of Malawi.
1966 - Malawi became a republic within the Commonwealth with Dr Hastings Banda as its first president.
1967 - Civil war erupted in Nigeria.
1971 - Jazz musician Louis Armstrong died. His groups, the Hot Five and Hot Seven, from 1925 to 1927, had a revolutionary impact on jazz.
1973 - Otto Klemperer, German conductor particularly known for his interpretations of Beethoven, died.
1975 - The Comoros Islands parliament declared unilateral independence from French rule.
1988 - The world's worst offshore accident occurred when the Piper Alpha oil platform exploded in the British sector of the North Sea, killing 167 people.
1990 - Bulgarian President Petar Mladenov resigned after charges that he called for tanks to crush an anti-government protest.
1992 - Nigeria's social democrats won control of both houses of a new civilian parliament in army-supervised elections.
1994 - Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin pleaded for time and PLO chairman Yasser Arafat pleaded for money when they shared a platform in Paris to receive a United Nations peace prize.
1994 - President Bill Clinton became the first U.S. leader to visit the former Soviet Baltic republics.
1995 - A Milan judge ordered some of the top names in Italian fashion, including Giorgio Armani, Gianfranco Ferre and Krizia, to stand trial on corruption charges.
